scenario_description: Riverbend Market is likely to have a recurring surplus of packaged bread at closing, but the normal markdown process is still underway and no intervention is justified from the first observation alone. Later, Rose City Food Share offers to add Riverbend to an existing Wednesday evening pickup route that already passes the store, provided there are at least eight sealed, dated loaves. Once the projected surplus and compatible route are connected, the opportunity is sufficiently observable before the final Event. Greg then approves a no-cost pilot, and the final Event adds a same-evening reply cutoff. Proactively sending the available count and pickup details to Rose City Food Share, adding the pickup to the shift schedule, and recording a brief handoff for the closing team would turn routine surplus into a useful community donation without disrupting store operations.

parameter.subject: Wednesday food pickup route now passes Riverbend Market
parameter.body: Our Wednesday evening food-recovery route now passes Riverbend Market around 9:15 PM. We can collect at least eight sealed, dated loaves or similar packaged bakery items at no charge. Adding a store only requires a reply with the available count, pickup address, and on-duty contact name; items can be handed to the driver at the front entrance.

parameter.content: I am fine with trying the Rose City Food Share pickup tonight if they can use the marked-down bread. There is no fee, and the closing cashier can hand sealed loaves to the driver at the front entrance. Please keep it to a one-night pilot for now and note the final count in the shift record.

parameter.subject: Space available on tonight's Riverbend route
parameter.body: A pickup canceled, so tonight's driver has room for Riverbend's packaged bread. Reply by 7:45 PM with the count, Riverbend Market's address, and the on-duty contact, and we can include a 9:15 PM stop. If tonight does not work, the route will pass nearby again next Wednesday.

parameter.name: Rose City Food Share
parameter.notes: Collects sealed, dated surplus food from Portland businesses.
